title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an AI-enabled impersonation fraud. Scammers generated synthetic images and videos of a real, named attorney and used them to build hundreds of fake social media profiles offering immigration legal services. The AI-generated material was credible enough that prospective clients contacted the real attorney's office, indicating the synthetic content passed casual inspection by ordinary viewers.

The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI deployment. The AI tools were used by outside actors to fabricate identity, not by a company deploying a system for a stated purpose. The gap that allowed harm was the absence of any verification layer between a social media profile claiming to represent a licensed attorney and the vulnerable people who relied on it. Catching this would have required either platform-level detection of synthetic media at upload, or a mechanism for professionals to pre-register their likeness so impersonation attempts could be flagged automatically. Neither was present at scale, and removal only began after the real attorney engaged a third-party anti-piracy firm.

It is not established who the perpetrators are, where they operate, or whether any legal action has produced findings against them. The losses reported are based on victim accounts and the attorney's observations, not on any official investigation or verified financial audit.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of a sophisticated scam using artificial intelligence. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal, offering immigration services he never provides. The scammers use these videos to convince vulnerable immigrants to pay thousands of dollars, with one video falsely claiming to offer US residency assistance for $2,200. Leal discovered the fraud when potential clients began calling his office, and he estimates the problem has dramatically worsened over the past three months.

To combat the fraud, Leal's firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact a WhatsApp number, where perpetrators send phony contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the matter. He is warning immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to avoid anyone requesting immediate payment through money transfer apps.
